length.text: Usually about 1 m; large ones about 1.9 m

overview.text: The Puff Adder is a thick-bodied viper found across most of Africa and in south-western Arabia. It is thought to cause more snakebite deaths than any other African snake - because it is so widespread, often lives near people, and is quick to bite when disturbed.

size.label: Typical adults
size.text: Usually about 1 m in total length.

size.label: Largest
size.text: Big specimens reach around 190 cm. Snakes from Saudi Arabia are smaller, usually under 80 cm.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Most of Africa except the Sahara and the rainforests, plus south-western Arabia (Saudi Arabia, Yemen and possibly southern Oman).

habitat.text: Open country such as savanna and grassland.

behaviour.text: Named for the way it hisses and puffs itself up when approached.

reproduction.text: Gives birth to live young. Very large females, especially from East Africa, have the biggest litters: a female from Kenya kept in a Czech zoo gave birth to 156 babies, the largest litter recorded for any snake.

funfacts.text: A Puff Adder holds the record for the most babies born at once to any snake: 156.
